name: Naturalisation (regular way of acquiring Croatian citizenship)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 8 years of continuous, registered residence in Croatia immediately preceding the application, holding approved permanent-resident (stalni boravak) status.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 8 years' continuous registered residence in Croatia under permanent-resident status.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires knowledge of the Croatian language, Latin script, culture, and social organisation, tested at a minimum of B1. Applicants over 60 are exempt.
requirements.fix_path: Pass the Croatian language/culture examination at B1, or qualify for the over-60 exemption.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires either being released from prior citizenship or providing proof it will be granted upon acquiring Croatian citizenship.
Requires respecting Croatia's legal system, having settled all due public obligations, and posing no security barrier to acceptance.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 8 years' continuous registered residence under permanent-resident status
Croatian language, script, and culture examination certificate (or over-60 exemption evidence)
Proof of release from prior citizenship, or a guarantee it will be granted
Certificate confirming no security barriers / settled public obligations

sources.title: Ministarstvo unutarnjih poslova Republike Hrvatske (mup.gov.hr) -- What is the regular way of acquiring Croatian citizenship?

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Croatia's initial build. This resolves an earlier sourcing gap in this research pass: the specific '8 years' residency figure was initially found only via zakon.hr (a private legal database, tier-3/4), then independently confirmed at tier-1 directly on mup.gov.hr's own naturalisation-conditions page -- now cited as the sole source, and zakon.hr is not used. prerequisites points to hr_permanent_stay because the source explicitly requires 'odobren status stranca na stalnom boravku' (approved permanent-resident/stalni-boravak status) held for the full 8 years, not merely any legal residence. dual_citizenship_allowed is set to false based on the explicit renunciation/release requirement -- a real substantive condition of this Act, unlike Estonia and Barbados where this was left null for lack of a clear tier-1 statement. HONEST GAP, DELIBERATE SCOPE DECISION: gov.hr separately lists 'Marriage/Civil Partnership' as its own naturalisation ground alongside ordinary residence, implying a possibly-reduced residence period for spouses of Croatian citizens (commonly cited in secondary/tier-3/4 sources as around 3 years, sometimes with no residence test in some interpretations) -- this pass could NOT find a tier-1 source stating the actual reduced figure or conditions, so no separate 'spouse' requirement group was built here rather than invent one. This is a genuine open question for this country, flagged the same way Barbados' unconfirmed marriage/descent citizenship grounds were flagged -- revisit if a tier-1 source for the marriage-based track surfaces. Citizenship by descent/origin and by diaspora/emigrant status are modelled as separate routes (hr_citizenship_descent, hr_citizenship_diaspora) since they are genuinely different legal grounds requiring no residence test at all, not variants of this route.
